email.body1:
Jeff, saw Esper made Inc.'s 2026 fastest-growing list and added Windows support to go after mixed-fleet device management.

Moving into mixed fleets usually means more accounts in play than the team can cover before reps learn the expanded story, and that is where deals stall. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Esper off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress ~4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Jeff, quick follow-up for Esper.

Fast growth plus a broader product usually means the target grows faster than the team can cover. Most teams do not actually know how many meetings they need to hit the new number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Esper needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Jeff, last bit of proof for Esper.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks with every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Esper's reply rate likely compares to other infrastructure software teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through it?
